sentences.text: FACTS OF THE CASE 1.

Briefly stated, the facts of the petition are that on 22.07.2023, at about 11:30 p.m., the petitioner/injured namely Subhash Chandra was riding pillion along with his companion Himanshu on motorcycle bearing registration no. DL5SCJ-7492.

It has been alleged that when they reached in front of PNB Bank, GT Road, Shree Ram Nagar, Shahdara, Delhi, a Bike bearing registration no.
DL1SAF-7376 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle), came at a high speed and hit the bike of the petitioner as aforesaid with a great force.

It has been further alleged that the offending vehicle was being driven by its driver i.e. respondent no. 1 (R1) herein, at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner without taking due caution at the time of the accident, due to which the petitioner received grievous injuries.
Allegedly, the injured/petitioner was thereon taken to GTB Hospital for primary treatment, where his MLC was prepared vide MLC no. 5440/50/2023.
The injured thereafter took further treatment from Pushpanjali Hospital, Karkardooma, Delhi.
An FIR bearing no. 234/2023, PS M S Park, for the offences u/s 279/338 IPC also came to be registered against the driver of the offending vehicle.

Finally, the present DAR came HARUN PRATAP Date:

insurance company vide policy no. 3397/02892183/000/00 in the name of respondent no. 2, with its validity from 06.10.2022 to 06.10.2026 and that the driver was having a valid driving license at the time of accident.

In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is tested on the touchstone of principle of preponderance of probabilities.

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or Digitally signed by HARUN HARUN PRATAP PRATAP

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is in fact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi &
Ors. Vs Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530,
which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs Amir Chand & Ors, 2011 (1) SCR 1906 (Civil Appeal No. 1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

Both the afore-said witnesses have categorically stated in their examination on oath that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent act of respondent no. 1 in driving the offending vehicle.

The testimony of both the witnesses for the petitioner has remained consistent and no doubt has been raised by the respondents to disbelieve the same.
13.

Herein the present case, the fact that the offending vehicle had hit the petitioner from the front side is ipso-facto sufficient proof of rash and negligent act on part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The very fact that R-1 has already been specifically arrayed as an accused in case FIR No. 234/23, PS M S Park, for the offences u/s 279/338 IPC is also a strong circumstance to support the above said testimony of PW-1 and PW2 on these issues.
At the same time, it is an admitted fact on record that the R1 has been charge-sheeted in the criminal case pertaining to the incident in question.

The position of law in this regard has been made clear in the case of "National Insurance Co., Vs Puspha Rana", 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, wherein it has been held that filing of Chargesheet is sufficient proof of the negligence and involvement of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: 16. Having ruled so, this Tribunal now proceeds to assess the wrongful act, neglect or default of R-1, if any, in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

Admittedly,
R-1 has not explained the circumstances under which his vehicle (i.e. the offending vehicle) hit the injured.

In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the injured, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

In view of the above HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:
2025.09.02 15:23:10 +0530 discussion, this Tribunal is constrained to hold R-1 guilty of gross neglect and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time leading to the injuries to the petitioner.
17. In view of the medical treatment documents placed on record by the petitioner, no dispute is left regarding the grievous injuries sustained by him in the incident in question.

18. Therefore, in view of the above discussion, this Tribunal has no hesitation in hereby arriving at the finding that the petitioner suffered grievous injuries on his person on account of neglect and default of R-1 while driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
The issue at hand thus hereby stands decided against the respondents and in favour of the petitioner accordingly.
Issue no. (ii) Whether petitioner is entitled to compensation?

The respondent no. 1 Mohd. Yunus is the principal tort feasor being driver, while the respondent no. 2 is vicariously liable being the owner of the offending vehicle.

At the same time, the respondent no. 3 has failed to bring on record or to prove any breach of the terms or conditions of the said insurance policy by the respondents no. 1 and 2 in any manner.

22. Hence, on the basis of entire above stated facts and circumstances and discussion of evidence,
this Tribunal is of the opinion that respondent no.3 i.e. insurance company, is liable to pay the entire compensation to the petitioner on behalf of respondent no. 1 and 2, without any recovery rights.
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 23.

At this stage, while the Tribunal was pronouncing its judgment at the final stage, all the parties submitted that they have amicably settled the quantum of compensation for an amount of Rs.
3,00,000/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Only) to be paid by R3 i.e. insurance company.
Separate statement of the petitioner and the counsel for respondent no. 3 also recorded to this effect.

The Tribunal is satisfied that the aforesaid settlement regarding quantum of compensation payable in this case has been arrived between the HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:

Hence, in order to finally put the matter to rest and to give it a complete finality, the aforesaid amount of Rs. 3,00,000/- is hereby awarded as full and final compensation to be granted in favour of the petitioner in this case.

In view of the findings on the aforesaid issues, the petitioner is hereby awarded a sum of Rs.
3,00,000/- (Rupees Three Lakh only) to be payable by respondent no. R3 i.e. insurance company to the petitioner.
